questions.prompt: Explain the role of AnyCancellable and what happens if it is not stored. Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that AnyCancellable manages the active lifetime of a subscription
Explains that if not stored, the token deallocates on scope exit, calling cancel() and terminating the stream

questions.modelAnswer: AnyCancellable represents the active lifetime of a Combine subscription. If you do not store the returned AnyCancellable token in a property or Set, it deallocates immediately when the local function scope ends. Its deinitializer automatically calls cancel(), terminating the subscription before asynchronous values can arrive.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between PassthroughSubject and CurrentValueSubject. Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that PassthroughSubject broadcasts events without buffering past values for late subscribers
Explains that CurrentValueSubject stores an initial/current value and replays it immediately to new subscribers

questions.modelAnswer: PassthroughSubject broadcasts events to active subscribers without storing or buffering past elements, meaning new subscribers only receive future events. In contrast, CurrentValueSubject requires an initial value and retains its latest element in memory. Any new subscriber immediately receives the current value upon connecting.

questions.prompt: Why can assign(to:on: self) cause a retain cycle and how can you fix it? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that assign(to:on:) creates a strong reference to self, which forms a retain cycle when self holds the returned cancellable
Explains fixing the leak using sink with [weak self] or assign(to: &$property) with @Published

questions.modelAnswer: The operator assign(to:on: self) holds a strong reference to the target instance. If that same instance stores the returned AnyCancellable in a property, a strong reference cycle is created (self -> cancellable -> self). To prevent memory leaks, developers should use sink with a [weak self] capture list or use assign(to: &$property) on @Published properties.

questions.prompt: Explain the purpose of the debounce operator and provide a practical iOS example. Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that debounce pauses emissions until a specified quiet duration passes without new events
Provides a practical example such as search text input to avoid firing network requests on every single keystroke

questions.modelAnswer: The debounce operator waits for a specified time interval of quiet activity before emitting the latest value downstream. A practical iOS example is a search bar where users type rapidly. Debouncing by 300 milliseconds waits until the user pauses typing before initiating a search network request, avoiding dozens of redundant API calls.

questions.prompt: How does Combine compare with Swift Concurrency AsyncStream for handling asynchronous event sequences? Answer in 2–5 sentences.
questions.lessonSection: How to answer in the interview

rubric.criterion: Explains that Swift Concurrency uses native language features (async/await and AsyncStream) prioritized for modern Swift code
Explains that Combine remains vital for existing production codebases, older UIKit architectures, and complex functional operator pipelines

questions.modelAnswer: Modern Swift prioritizes native language concurrency using async/await and AsyncStream, which integrate directly into Swift 6 task isolation and structured concurrency. However, Combine remains essential for supporting existing production codebases, reactive UIKit view models, and advanced multi-stream operator pipelines. Both frameworks co-exist effectively across iOS development.
